The PostgreSQL driver now ensures `DateStyle=ISO` on every connection it uses. A connection Prisma opens from a URL starts with it as a startup option, after any `options` in the URL or `PGOPTIONS`. On a `pg.Pool` or `pg.Client` you pass to Prisma, the driver sets it with one statement on each connection before first use, and again after a connection held for a transaction, an ORM operation or a Supabase role scope is released. Nothing needs changing for either.

Remove any statement that sets a `DateStyle` other than `ISO` on a connection Prisma uses, such as a `SET DateStyle` in a pool's `connect` handler or in raw SQL: every date and time codec that reads a date or timestamp (text, `Temporal` or `Date`) refuses text in another style with `RUNTIME.DATE_STYLE_NOT_ISO`. Behind a connection pooler that refuses startup options, pass Prisma your own `pg.Pool` instead of a URL; behind one that runs each statement on another server connection, also run `ALTER ROLE <role> SET DateStyle = 'ISO'` (or set it on the database).

## Field presets are removed

This section replaces two pieces of advice from the 8.0.0-rc.19 upgrade guide. That guide said that `field.generated(...)` keeps working for now, and that a field preset keeps its `number`, `option` and `object` arguments. Neither holds any more: this release removes `field.generated(...)` and every field preset, in PSL and in TypeScript, and the tables below give what to write instead.

A field preset was a call in a field's type position that set the column, the identity and the generated values at once, such as `id.uuidv4String()` or `temporal.createdAt()`. Each is now written with what the rest of a contract uses: a type constructor or a contributed alias, such as `Ulid` or `temporal.CreatedAt`, plus `@id`, `@onCreate(...)` and `@onUpdate(...)` in PSL, or `.id()`, `.onCreate(gen.fn())` and `.onUpdate(gen.fn())` in TypeScript. Every replacement stores the same contract as its preset, with the same storage and execution hashes. So after the rewrite nothing is re-emitted, signed or migrated: `prisma contract emit` writes the `contract.json` you have. Rewrite the calls where your project's comments and documentation show them too, such as a README, in PSL and in TypeScript; the detections look only at `.prisma` and TypeScript files.

```prisma
// Before
model Event {
  id        id.uuidv4String()
  code      nanoid({ size: 12 })
  seenAt    temporal.time(3, onUpdate: now)
  createdAt temporal.createdAt()
  payload   json()
}

// After
model Event {
  id        UuidString         @id @onCreate(uuid())
  code      Char(12)
  seenAt    Time(3)            @onUpdate(now())
  createdAt temporal.CreatedAt
  payload   Jsonb
}
```

```ts
// Before
({ field, model }) => ({
  models: {
    Event: model('Event', {
      fields: {
        id: field.id.uuidv4String(),
        code: field.nanoid({ size: 12 }),
        seenAt: field.temporal.time(3, undefined, 'now'),
        createdAt: field.temporal.createdAt(),
        payload: field.json(),
        slug: field.generated(nanoid({ size: 16 })),
      },
    }),
  },
})

// After
({ field, model, gen, type }) => ({
  models: {
    Event: model('Event', {
      fields: {
        id: field.column(type.UuidString()).id().onCreate(gen.uuid()),
        code: field.column(type.Char(12)),
        seenAt: field.column(type.Time(3)).onUpdate(gen.now()),
        createdAt: field.column(type.temporal.CreatedAt()),
        payload: field.column(type.Jsonb()),
        slug: field.column(type.Char(16)).onCreate(gen.nanoid(16)),
      },
    }),
  },
})
```

### The replacement of each preset

In the tables, a PSL preset is written as in a schema. Its TypeScript form is the same call on `field`: `id.uuidv4String()` is `field.id.uuidv4String()`, and `temporal.createdAt()` is `field.temporal.createdAt()`.

#### SQL family presets, on Postgres and SQLite

Each identifier preset is replaced by the type alias for its column: `UuidString`, `Ulid`, `Nanoid`, `Cuid2` or `Ksuid`. The field writes `@id` and `@onCreate(...)` itself where the preset set them. On Postgres, write the alias as a top-level name, `Ulid` in PSL and `type.Ulid()` in TypeScript, as the table does. On SQLite, write it in the `sql` namespace, `sql.Ulid` and `type.sql.Ulid()`. Both forms store the same column as `Char(26)`. A nanoid of another size has no alias, so its column is written out: `Char(n)` on Postgres, `sql.Char(n)` on SQLite.

| Preset | Stores | PSL replacement | TypeScript replacement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `uuidString()` | `sql/char@1`, `{ length: 36 }` | `UuidString` | `field.column(type.UuidString())` |
| `ulid()` | `sql/char@1`, `{ length: 26 }` | `Ulid` | `field.column(type.Ulid())` |
| `nanoid()` | `sql/char@1`, `{ length: 21 }` | `Nanoid` | `field.column(type.Nanoid())` |
| `nanoid({ size: n })` | `sql/char@1`, `{ length: n }` | `Char(n)` | `field.column(type.Char(n))` |
| `cuid2()` | `sql/char@1`, `{ length: 24 }` | `Cuid2` | `field.column(type.Cuid2())` |
| `ksuid()` | `sql/char@1`, `{ length: 27 }` | `Ksuid` | `field.column(type.Ksuid())` |
| `id.uuidv4String()` | as `uuidString()`, `@id`, `uuidv4` on create | `UuidString @id @onCreate(uuid())` | `field.column(type.UuidString()).id().onCreate(gen.uuid())` |
| `id.uuidv7String()` | as above, `uuidv7` | `UuidString @id @onCreate(uuid(7))` | `field.column(type.UuidString()).id().onCreate(gen.uuid(7))` |
| `id.ulid()` | `{ length: 26 }`, `@id`, `ulid` | `Ulid @id @onCreate(ulid())` | `field.column(type.Ulid()).id().onCreate(gen.ulid())` |
| `id.nanoid()` | `{ length: 21 }`, `@id`, `nanoid` | `Nanoid @id @onCreate(nanoid())` | `field.column(type.Nanoid()).id().onCreate(gen.nanoid())` |
| `id.nanoid({ size: n })` | `{ length: n }`, `@id`, `nanoid` of size `n` | `Char(n) @id @onCreate(nanoid(n))` | `field.column(type.Char(n)).id().onCreate(gen.nanoid(n))` |
| `id.cuid2()` | `{ length: 24 }`, `@id`, `cuid2` | `Cuid2 @id @onCreate(cuid(2))` | `field.column(type.Cuid2()).id().onCreate(gen.cuid(2))` |
| `id.ksuid()` | `{ length: 27 }`, `@id`, `ksuid` | `Ksuid @id @onCreate(ksuid())` | `field.column(type.Ksuid()).id().onCreate(gen.ksuid())` |

A foreign key that holds one of these identifiers uses the alias alone, as in `authorId Ulid`, because its value is copied from the row it points at.

A model, composite type or type alias your schema declares with an alias's name, such as `model Ulid`, hides the top-level alias: `Ulid` then names your declaration. Write `sql.Ulid` in that schema instead; it names the same column.

To write a generated id once, declare a mixin and include it with `+` in each model:

```prisma
model mixin UlidId {
  id Ulid @id @onCreate(ulid())
}

model Post {
  +UlidId
  authorId Ulid
  author   User @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])
}
```

In TypeScript, declare the field once and use it in each model. Declare it inside the `defineContract` callback, or with the `field`, `type` and `gen` that `@prisma/orm-postgres/contract-builder` exports:

```ts
const UlidId = field.column(type.Ulid()).id().onCreate(gen.ulid());
```

On Postgres, the native `Uuid` column stores a UUID in 16 bytes and is a better choice for a new schema, written `Uuid @id @onCreate(uuid(7))`. Moving an existing column from `UuidString` to `Uuid` changes the contract and needs a migration, so it is not part of this upgrade.

A TypeScript `id` preset's trailing `{ name }`, as in `field.id.uuidv4String({ name: 'user_pk' })`, moves to `.id({ name: 'user_pk' })`.

#### Postgres presets

| Preset | Stores | PSL replacement | TypeScript replacement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text()` | `pg/text@1` | `String` | `field.column(type.String())` |
| `int()` | `pg/int4@1` | `Int` | `field.column(type.Int())` |
| `bigint()` | `pg/int8@1` | `BigInt` | `field.column(type.BigInt())` |
| `float()` | `pg/float8@1` | `Float` | `field.column(type.Float())` |
| `decimal()` | `pg/numeric@1`, no parameters | `Decimal` | `field.column(type.Decimal())` |
| `boolean()` | `pg/bool@1` | `Boolean` | `field.column(type.Boolean())` |
| `json()` | `pg/jsonb@1` | `Jsonb` (not `Json`, which is `pg/json@1`) | `field.column(type.Jsonb())` |
| `bytes()` | `pg/bytea@1` | `Bytes` | `field.column(type.Bytes())` |
| `dateTime()` | `pg/timestamptz-temporal@1` | `DateTime` | `field.column(type.DateTime())` |
| `uuidNative()` | `pg/uuid@1` | `Uuid` | `field.column(type.Uuid())` |
| `id.uuidv4Native()` | `pg/uuid@1`, `@id`, `uuidv4` | `Uuid @id @onCreate(uuid())` | `field.column(type.Uuid()).id().onCreate(gen.uuid())` |
| `id.uuidv7Native()` | `pg/uuid@1`, `@id`, `uuidv7` | `Uuid @id @onCreate(uuid(7))` | `field.column(type.Uuid()).id().onCreate(gen.uuid(7))` |
| `temporal.createdAt()` | `pg/timestamptz-temporal@1`, now on create | `temporal.CreatedAt` | `field.column(type.temporal.CreatedAt())` |
| `temporal.updatedAt()` | the same, on create and update | `temporal.UpdatedAt` | `field.column(type.temporal.UpdatedAt())` |
| `temporal.createdAtString()`, `temporal.updatedAtString()` | `pg/timestamptz-string@1` | `temporal.CreatedAtString`, `temporal.UpdatedAtString` | `field.column(type.temporal.CreatedAtString())`, `field.column(type.temporal.UpdatedAtString())` |
| `temporal.createdAtJsDate()`, `temporal.updatedAtJsDate()` | `pg/timestamptz-date@1` | `temporal.CreatedAtJsDate`, `temporal.UpdatedAtJsDate` | `field.column(type.temporal.CreatedAtJsDate())`, `field.column(type.temporal.UpdatedAtJsDate())` |
| `temporal.timestamp(p, onCreate: now, onUpdate: now)` | `pg/timestamp-temporal@1`, `{ precision: p }` | `TimestampTemporal(p) @onCreate(now()) @onUpdate(now())` | `field.column(type.TimestampTemporal(p)).onCreate(gen.now()).onUpdate(gen.now())` |
| `temporal.timestamptz(...)` | `pg/timestamptz-temporal@1` | `TimestamptzTemporal(p)` and the attributes | `field.column(type.TimestamptzTemporal(p))` and the calls |
| `temporal.timestampString(...)` | `pg/timestamp-string@1` | `TimestampString(p)` and the attributes | `field.column(type.TimestampString(p))` and the calls |
| `temporal.timestamptzString(...)` | `pg/timestamptz-string@1` | `TimestamptzString(p)` and the attributes | `field.column(type.TimestamptzString(p))` and the calls |
| `temporal.timestamptzJsDate(...)` | `pg/timestamptz-date@1` | `TimestamptzJsDate(p)` and the attributes | `field.column(type.TimestamptzJsDate(p))` and the calls |
| `temporal.date(onCreate: now, onUpdate: now)` | `pg/date-temporal@1` | `Date` and the attributes | `field.column(type.Date())` and the calls |
| `temporal.dateString(...)` | `pg/date-string@1` | `DateString` and the attributes | `field.column(type.DateString())` and the calls |
| `temporal.time(p, ...)` | `pg/time-temporal@1` | `Time(p)` and the attributes | `field.column(type.Time(p))` and the calls |
| `temporal.timeString(p, ...)` | `pg/time-string@1` | `TimeString(p)` and the attributes | `field.column(type.TimeString(p))` and the calls |
| `temporal.timetz(p, ...)` | `pg/timetz@1` | `Timetz(p)` and the attributes | `field.column(type.Timetz(p))` and the calls |

The `temporal.<type>(...)` presets take an optional precision `p` (the first argument, or `precision: p`) and the phases `onCreate: now` and `onUpdate: now`. Write the precision as the constructor's argument, and leave it out when the preset left it out: `temporal.timestamptz()` is `TimestamptzTemporal`. Write each phase the preset set as its attribute, `@onCreate(now())` or `@onUpdate(now())`, and leave out a phase it did not set: `temporal.time(3, onUpdate: now)` is `Time(3) @onUpdate(now())`. A preset with no phase is the bare constructor.

In TypeScript the precision and the phases are positional, and a phase is `'now'` or `undefined`: `field.temporal.timestamp(3, 'now', 'now')` is `field.column(type.TimestampTemporal(3)).onCreate(gen.now()).onUpdate(gen.now())`, `field.temporal.time(3, undefined, 'now')` is `field.column(type.Time(3)).onUpdate(gen.now())`, and `field.temporal.date('now')` is `field.column(type.Date()).onCreate(gen.now())`.

Attributes and calls written after the preset stay after the replacement: `temporal.updatedAt() @map("updated_at")` is `temporal.UpdatedAt @map("updated_at")`, `field.temporal.createdAt().optional()` is `field.column(type.temporal.CreatedAt()).optional()`, and `temporal.timestamptz(onUpdate: now) @onCreate(now())` is `TimestamptzTemporal @onCreate(now()) @onUpdate(now())`.

#### SQLite presets

| Preset | Stores | PSL replacement | TypeScript replacement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `temporal.createdAt()`, `temporal.updatedAt()` | `sqlite/datetime@1`, now on create, and on update for `updatedAt` | `temporal.CreatedAt`, `temporal.UpdatedAt` | `field.column(type.temporal.CreatedAt())`, `field.column(type.temporal.UpdatedAt())` |
| `temporal.datetime(onCreate: now, onUpdate: now)` | `sqlite/datetime@1` | `DateTime @onCreate(now()) @onUpdate(now())` | `field.column(type.DateTime()).onCreate(gen.now()).onUpdate(gen.now())` |

The SQL family presets in the first table also existed on SQLite. Their replacements use the `sql.` aliases, such as `sql.Ulid` and `type.sql.Ulid()`, and `sql.Char(n)` and `type.sql.Char(n)` for a nanoid of another size.

#### MongoDB presets

| Preset | Stores | PSL replacement | TypeScript replacement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `temporal.createdAt()` | `mongo/date@1`, now on create | `temporal.CreatedAt` | `field.date().onCreate(gen.now())` |
| `temporal.updatedAt()` | the same, on create and update | `temporal.UpdatedAt` | `field.date().onCreate(gen.now()).onUpdate(gen.now())` |
| `temporal.timestamp(onCreate: now, onUpdate: now)` | `mongo/date@1` | `Date @onCreate(now()) @onUpdate(now())` | `field.date().onCreate(gen.now()).onUpdate(gen.now())` |

The MongoDB TypeScript builder has no `type` helpers, so its replacements use `field.date()`.

#### `field.generated(...)`, in the SQL TypeScript builder

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `field.generated(uuidv4())` | `field.column(type.UuidString()).onCreate(gen.uuid())` |
| `field.generated(uuidv7())` | `field.column(type.UuidString()).onCreate(gen.uuid(7))` |
| `field.generated(ulid())` | `field.column(type.Ulid()).onCreate(gen.ulid())` |
| `field.generated(nanoid())` | `field.column(type.Nanoid()).onCreate(gen.nanoid())` |
| `field.generated(nanoid({ size: n }))` | `field.column(type.Char(n)).onCreate(gen.nanoid(n))` |
| `field.generated(cuid2())` | `field.column(type.Cuid2()).onCreate(gen.cuid(2))` |
| `field.generated(ksuid())` | `field.column(type.Ksuid()).onCreate(gen.ksuid())` |

On SQLite write the `sql.` forms, such as `type.sql.Ulid()` and `type.sql.Char(n)`. A `.id()` after `field.generated(...)` stays `.id()` on the replacement.

### `psl-field-presets-removed`

Rewrite every preset call in your Prisma 8 schema files as the tables say. `prisma contract emit` refuses each one with `PSL_UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE` and the exact rewrite, one diagnostic per field:

```text
PSL_UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE: id.uuidv4String() was a field preset, and Prisma 8 removed field presets. Write UuidString @id @onCreate(uuid()).
PSL_UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE: temporal.time(3, onUpdate: now) was a field preset, and Prisma 8 removed field presets. Write Time(3) @onUpdate(now()).
```

The message writes the alias as the schema's target names it: `UuidString` on Postgres and `sql.UuidString` on SQLite. On Postgres you may write `sql.UuidString` too; both store the same column. If a preset was called with an argument it did not take, the message gives the type and tells you which attributes to add.

Run `prisma contract emit`. It writes the same `contract.json` and `contract.d.ts`, with the same hashes.

### `ts-field-presets-removed`

Rewrite every preset call in your TypeScript contract and query fragments as the tables say.

In a `defineContract` callback, take `type` and `gen` from the callback's argument where the rewritten fields use them. Add each missing name at the end of the destructuring, `gen` before `type`: `({ field, model })` becomes `({ field, model, gen, type })`, and `({ field, model, type })` becomes `({ field, model, type, gen })`. If you rename the callback's `field`, as in `({ field: f })`, a preset call is written `f.id.uuidv4String()`; the detection does not see it, so search for it yourself.

On Postgres, use the constructors in the Postgres table and the top-level aliases, such as `type.Ulid()`, for the SQL family presets. On SQLite, use the `sql.` aliases, such as `type.sql.Ulid()`. Code that does not know its target can write `type.sql.Ulid()` and `type.sql.Char(n)`, which every SQL target has.

If the file already has a binding named `type`, such as `import { type } from 'arktype'`, the callback's `type` hides it inside the callback. Rename one of them, as in `({ field, model, gen, type: t })`, if the callback uses both.

A contract that calls the `field` imported from a facade's `contract-builder` outside a callback needs `type` too. `@prisma/orm-postgres/contract-builder` exports it. The other facades do not, so move the models into the `defineContract` callback, `defineContract({}, ({ field, model, gen, type }) => ({ models: { ... } }))`, and remove `field` from the import.

A query fragment that declares its fields with the `field` exported by `@prisma/orm-postgres/contract-builder` imports `type` from the same entry:

```ts
// Before
import { field } from '@prisma/orm-postgres/contract-builder';

export const createdSince = (since: Temporal.Instant) =>
  db.orm.fragment({ createdAt: field.temporal.timestamptz() }, (rows) =>
    rows.where((row) => row.createdAt.gte(since)),
  );

// After
import { field, type } from '@prisma/orm-postgres/contract-builder';

export const createdSince = (since: Temporal.Instant) =>
  db.orm.fragment({ createdAt: field.column(type.TimestamptzTemporal()) }, (rows) =>
    rows.where((row) => row.createdAt.gte(since)),
  );
```

A fragment field matches a column by its codec and nullability, so the replacement matches the same models the preset did.

In MongoDB contracts, `field.temporal.*` is the only preset. Take `gen` from the callback and write `field.date()` with `.onCreate(gen.now())` and `.onUpdate(gen.now())`. Leave `field.json()`, `field.date()`, `field.string()` and the other MongoDB field helpers alone; they are not presets.

Then type-check the project and run `prisma contract emit`. The contract does not change.

### `ts-field-generated-removed`

Replace each `field.generated(...)` as the table says, and remove `uuidv4`, `uuidv7`, `ulid`, `nanoid`, `cuid2` and `ksuid` from your imports of `@prisma/orm-framework/ids`. Remove the import if nothing is left in it. Take `gen` and `type` from the callback, as for `ts-field-presets-removed`. The contract does not change.

### `postgres-contract-builder-exports-type`

There is nothing to change. `@prisma/orm-postgres/contract-builder` exports `type` beside `field` and `gen`. Use it to declare the fields of a query fragment, as shown above.

### `sqlite-sql-char`

There is nothing to change. `sql.Char(n)` in PSL and `type.sql.Char(n)` in TypeScript are new on every SQL target and store `sql/char@1` with `{ length: n }`. A SQLite contract emitted from a nanoid preset of another size already stores this column, so rewriting the preset as `sql.Char(n)` keeps the contract.

### `identifier-type-aliases`

There is nothing to change. The identifier aliases are new: `sql.UuidString`, `sql.Ulid`, `sql.Nanoid`, `sql.Cuid2` and `sql.Ksuid` on every SQL target, and `UuidString`, `Ulid`, `Nanoid`, `Cuid2` and `Ksuid` on Postgres. Each stores `sql/char@1` with the length of its format, so `Ulid` and `Char(26)` store the same column with the same hashes. A schema that already writes `Char(26)` can keep it or switch to `Ulid`.

## A Prisma 7 `@default(now())` is written by the client on create

### `prisma7-schema-now-default-writes-on-create`

Prisma 7's client filled a `@default(now())` field itself on create, with the current time in UTC, and also wrote `now()` as the column default for inserts from outside Prisma. A contract from `prisma7Schema(...)` used to keep only the column default, so a create through Prisma 8 got the database's clock. On a `timestamp` column, that is the wall-clock time of the session's time zone, which differs from what Prisma 7 wrote unless the session runs in UTC.

The contract now keeps the column default and adds the `now` generator on create, chosen for the column's type:

```prisma
// Prisma 7 schema, read by prisma7Schema('prisma/schema.prisma')
model Post {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
}
```

reads as the Prisma 8 PSL field `createdAt TimestampString(3) @default(now()) @onCreate(now())`. A create that supplies `createdAt` still stores the supplied value. An `INSERT` from outside Prisma still gets the column default.

For each project whose `prisma.config.ts` uses `prisma7Schema(...)`, run `prisma contract emit` again and commit the new `contract.json` and `contract.d.ts`. If the schema has a `@default(now())` field, the generator's id is in the execution section of `contract.json`, so the execution hash changes. The storage hash does not change, and the database marker holds only the storage and profile hashes, so there is no migration to plan and no need to run `prisma db sign`.

If the schema has no `@default(now())` field, the contract does not change and there is nothing to do.

## `contract-artifacts-restamp`

For every `contract.json` matched by `detection`, run the project's emit command (`prisma contract emit`, or the project's `contract:emit` script) once after upgrading. This entry accounts for the extension's embedded `version` moving to `8.0.0-rc.21`; any other difference in the emitted files comes from an earlier entry in this guide.
````

## File: backend/.cursor/skills/prisma-8/upgrading/app/upgrades/8.0.0-rc.21-to-8.0.0-rc.22/scripts/value-objects-in-storage/value-objects-in-storage.ts
````typescript
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Moves the value objects of every SQL and MongoDB contract from the domain plane into storage. Contracts emitted before this release keep value objects at `domain.namespaces.<ns>.valueObjects` and type a field holding one as `{ kind: 'valueObject', name }`; this release keeps them at `storage.namespaces.<ns>.entries.valueObject` and types the field by the value object's storage coordinate. In each contract the script moves every value object into the storage namespace of the same id, points every field at it by coordinate, and points a member typed by an enum at the enum's storage value set. In a SQL contract it also writes the value set of each discriminator, keyed `<Base>.<field>` and holding the variants' values, and points the discriminator column at it, unless an enum already types that column. It makes the same changes in `contract.d.ts`.
 *
 * Storage now holds the value objects, so each rewritten contract has a new storage hash. The script renames each snapshot directory to its new hash and rewrites every migration, ref, `migration.ts` and `contract.d.ts` that names an old hash, and each migration's `migrationHash`. It does not add the checks PostgreSQL now derives for value object and discriminator columns: a snapshot records what its migrations created, and they created no such check. The next `prisma migration plan` adds them.
 *
 * Usage: node value-objects-in-storage.ts [project-root]
 *
 * The project root defaults to the working directory. The script reads and writes files only. It needs no database, network or configured stack, and a project whose contracts keep no value object in the domain plane is left unchanged. When it stops (a file it must read is not valid JSON, a contract whose stored hash does not match its content, a field naming a value object the contract does not declare, a value object whose namespace storage does not have, a member enum without a storage value set, a discriminator value set that already exists, a snapshot directory that already exists with different content, or a directory it cannot read) it changes no file, prints one line per case and exits 1. When it finishes it prints how many files and snapshot directories it changed and each storage hash it replaced.
 *
 * The storage hash and migration hash rules are copied from `@internal/contract`, `@internal/sql-contract`, `@internal/mongo-contract` and `@internal/migration-tools` because a project's strict `node_modules` does not expose them.
 */
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import {
  chmodSync,
  type Dirent,
  existsSync,
  mkdirSync,
  readdirSync,
  readFileSync,
  realpathSync,
  renameSync,
  rmSync,
  statSync,
  writeFileSync,
} from 'node:fs';
import { basename, dirname, join, relative, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';

type Json = null | boolean | number | string | Json[] | JsonRecord;
interface JsonRecord {
  [key: string]: Json;
}

type Family = 'sql' | 'mongo';

const SKIPPED_DIRECTORIES = new Set(['node_modules', 'dist', 'build']);
const HASH = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/;
const TEMPORARY_SUFFIX = '.value-objects-in-storage-tmp';
const BYTE_ORDER_MARK = '\uFEFF';

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is JsonRecord {
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) return false;
  const prototype: unknown = Object.getPrototypeOf(value);
  return prototype === Object.prototype || prototype === null;
}

function withoutByteOrderMark(text: string): string {
  return text.startsWith(BYTE_ORDER_MARK) ? text.slice(BYTE_ORDER_MARK.length) : text;
}

function parseJson(text: string): Json | undefined {
  try {
    const value: Json = JSON.parse(withoutByteOrderMark(text));
    return value;
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
}

function sha256(text: string): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex');
}

function compareCodeUnits(a: string, b: string): number {
  return a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0;
}

function sortKeys(value: Json): Json {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(sortKeys);
  if (!isRecord(value)) return value;
  const sorted: JsonRecord = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(value).sort(compareCodeUnits)) {
    const child = value[key];
    if (child !== undefined) sorted[key] = sortKeys(child);
  }
  return sorted;
}

function canonicalizeJson(value: Json): string {
  return JSON.stringify(sortKeys(value));
}

type PathSegment = string | readonly string[];

function matchesPath(path: readonly string[], pattern: readonly PathSegment[]): boolean {
  if (path.length !== pattern.length) return false;
  return pattern.every((segment, index) => {
    const value = path[index];
    if (value === undefined) return false;
    if (segment === '*') return true;
    return typeof segment === 'string' ? value === segment : segment.includes(value);
  });
}

const SQL_PRESERVED_EMPTY: readonly (readonly PathSegment[])[] = [
  ['storage', 'namespaces', '*', 'entries', 'table'],
  ['storage', 'namespaces', '*', 'entries', 'table', '*'],
  ['storage', 'namespaces', '*', 'entries', 'table', '*', ['uniques', 'indexes', 'foreignKeys']],
  ['storage', 'namespaces', '*', 'entries', 'table', '*', 'indexes', 'unique'],
  ['storage', 'namespaces', '*', 'entries', 'table', '*', 'columns', '*', 'default', 'value'],
];
const COLUMN_DEFAULT_VALUE: readonly PathSegment[] = [
  'storage',
  'namespaces',
  '*',
  'entries',
  'table',
  '*',
  'columns',
  '*',
  'default',
  'value',
];
const MONGO_PRESERVED_EMPTY: readonly (readonly PathSegment[])[] = [
  ['storage', 'namespaces', '*', 'entries', 'collection'],
  ['storage', 'namespaces', '*', 'entries', 'collection', '*'],
];
const FRAMEWORK_PRESERVED_EMPTY: readonly (readonly PathSegment[])[] = [
  ['domain', 'namespaces'],
  ['domain', 'namespaces', '*'],
  ['domain', 'namespaces', '*', 'models'],
  ['domain', 'namespaces', '*', 'models', '*', 'relations'],
  ['domain', 'namespaces', '*', 'models', '*', 'storage'],
  ['storage', 'namespaces'],
  ['storage', 'namespaces', '*', 'entries'],
  ['roots'],
  ['extensions'],
  ['extensions', '*'],
  ['capabilities'],
  ['meta'],
  ['execution', 'mutations', 'defaults'],
];
const TOP_LEVEL_ORDER = [
  'schemaVersion',
  'canonicalVersion',
  'targetFamily',
  'target',
  'profileHash',
  'roots',
  'domain',
  'storage',
  'execution',
  'capabilities',
  'extensions',
  'defaultControlPolicy',
  'meta',
];

function isDefaultValue(value: Json): boolean {
  if (value === false) return true;
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.length === 0;
  return isRecord(value) && Object.keys(value).length === 0;
}

function isFamilyPreservedEmpty(family: Family, path: readonly string[]): boolean {
  if (family === 'mongo') {
    return (
      path.at(-1) === 'additionalProperties' ||
      (path.includes('jsonSchema') && (path.at(-2) === 'properties' || path.at(-1) === 'items')) ||
      MONGO_PRESERVED_EMPTY.some((pattern) => matchesPath(path, pattern))
    );
  }
  if (
    path.length >= COLUMN_DEFAULT_VALUE.length &&
    matchesPath(path.slice(0, COLUMN_DEFAULT_VALUE.length), COLUMN_DEFAULT_VALUE)
  )
    return true;
  return SQL_PRESERVED_EMPTY.some((pattern) => matchesPath(path, pattern));
}

function isPreservedEmpty(family: Family, path: readonly string[], key: string): boolean {
  if (key === 'nullable') return true;
  if (key === 'elementNullable' && path.at(-2) === 'many') return true;
  if (FRAMEWORK_PRESERVED_EMPTY.some((pattern) => matchesPath(path, pattern))) return true;
  return isFamilyPreservedEmpty(family, path);
}

function omitDefaults(family: Family, value: Json, path: readonly string[]): Json {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map((item) => omitDefaults(family, item, path));
  if (!isRecord(value)) return value;
  const result: JsonRecord = {};
  for (const [key, child] of Object.entries(value)) {
    const childPath = [...path, key];
    if (key === '_generated') continue;
    if (key === 'generated' && child === false) continue;
    if ((key === 'onDelete' || key === 'onUpdate') && child === 'noAction') continue;
    if (isDefaultValue(child) && !isPreservedEmpty(family, childPath, key)) continue;
    result[key] = omitDefaults(family, child, childPath);
  }
  return result;
}

function compareByName(a: Json, b: Json): number {
  const nameA = isRecord(a) && typeof a['name'] === 'string' ? a['name'] : '';
  const nameB = isRecord(b) && typeof b['name'] === 'string' ? b['name'] : '';
  return compareCodeUnits(nameA, nameB);
}

function sortTableArrays(storage: Json): Json {
  if (!isRecord(storage)) return storage;
  const namespaces = storage['namespaces'];
  if (!isRecord(namespaces)) return storage;
  const sortedNamespaces: JsonRecord = {};
  for (const [namespaceId, namespace] of Object.entries(namespaces)) {
    const entries = isRecord(namespace) ? namespace['entries'] : undefined;
    const tables = isRecord(entries) ? entries['table'] : undefined;
    if (!isRecord(namespace) || !isRecord(entries) || !isRecord(tables)) {
      sortedNamespaces[namespaceId] = namespace;
      continue;
    }
    const sortedTables: JsonRecord = {};
    for (const [tableName, table] of Object.entries(tables)) {
      if (!isRecord(table)) {
        sortedTables[tableName] = table;
        continue;
      }
      const sortedTable: JsonRecord = { ...table };
      for (const key of ['checks', 'indexes', 'uniques']) {
        const list = table[key];
        if (Array.isArray(list)) sortedTable[key] = [...list].sort(compareByName);
      }
      sortedTables[tableName] = sortedTable;
    }
    sortedNamespaces[namespaceId] = { ...namespace, entries: { ...entries, table: sortedTables } };
  }
  return { ...storage, namespaces: sortedNamespaces };
}

function orderTopLevel(value: JsonRecord): JsonRecord {
  const ordered: JsonRecord = {};
  const remaining = new Set(Object.keys(value));
  for (const key of TOP_LEVEL_ORDER) {
    const child = value[key];
    if (child !== undefined) {
      ordered[key] = child;
      remaining.delete(key);
    }
  }
  for (const key of [...remaining].sort(compareCodeUnits)) {
    const child = value[key];
    if (child !== undefined) ordered[key] = child;
  }
  return ordered;
}

function omitNamespaceKinds(storage: JsonRecord): JsonRecord {
  const namespaces = storage['namespaces'];
  if (!isRecord(namespaces)) return storage;
  const stripped: JsonRecord = {};
  for (const [namespaceId, namespace] of Object.entries(namespaces)) {
    if (isRecord(namespace)) {
      const { kind: _kind, ...rest } = namespace;
      stripped[namespaceId] = rest;
    } else {
      stripped[namespaceId] = namespace;
    }
  }
  return { ...storage, namespaces: stripped };
}

function computeStorageHash(family: Family, contract: JsonRecord): string {
  const storage = isRecord(contract['storage']) ? contract['storage'] : {};
  const { storageHash: _published, ...withoutHash } = storage;
  const hashed: JsonRecord = {
    schemaVersion: '1',
    targetFamily: typeof contract['targetFamily'] === 'string' ? contract['targetFamily'] : '',
    target: typeof contract['target'] === 'string' ? contract['target'] : '',
    profileHash: '',
    roots: {},
    domain: { namespaces: {} },
    storage: omitNamespaceKinds(withoutHash),
    extensions: {},
    capabilities: {},
    meta: {},
  };
  const withoutDefaults = omitDefaults(family, hashed, []);
  if (!isRecord(withoutDefaults)) return '';
  const withSortedStorage =
    family === 'sql'
      ? { ...withoutDefaults, storage: sortTableArrays(withoutDefaults['storage'] ?? {}) }
      : withoutDefaults;
  const sorted = sortKeys(withSortedStorage);
  return isRecord(sorted) ? sha256(JSON.stringify(orderTopLevel(sorted), null, 2)) : '';
}

function computeMigrationHash(metadata: JsonRecord, ops: Json): string {
  const { migrationHash: _migrationHash, ...withoutHash } = metadata;
  const parts = [canonicalizeJson(withoutHash), canonicalizeJson(ops)].map(sha256);
  return sha256(canonicalizeJson(parts));
}

interface ProjectFiles {
  readonly json: readonly string[];
  readonly migrationJson: readonly string[];
  readonly refs: readonly string[];
  readonly migrationTs: readonly string[];
  readonly leftovers: readonly string[];
  readonly unreadable: readonly { readonly dir: string; readonly code: string }[];
}

function isDirectory(path: string): boolean {
  try {
    return statSync(path).isDirectory();
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

function isFile(path: string): boolean {
  try {
    return statSync(path).isFile();
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/** A file, or a link to one: the script reads and writes through links to files. */
function isFileEntry(dir: string, entry: Dirent): boolean {
  return entry.isFile() || (entry.isSymbolicLink() && isFile(join(dir, entry.name)));
}

/** A file the script reads, by the path it was reached through: its own path rather than a link's. */
interface FoundFile {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly linked: boolean;
  readonly inMigrationPackage: boolean;
}

function listFiles(root: string): ProjectFiles {
  const leftovers: string[] = [];
  const visited = new Set<string>();
  const found = new Map<string, FoundFile>();
  const unreadable: { dir: string; code: string }[] = [];
  const visit = (dir: string): void => {
    const realDir = realpathSync(dir);
    if (visited.has(realDir)) return;
    visited.add(realDir);
    const listed = listDirectory(dir);
    if (!listed.ok) {
      unreadable.push({ dir, code: listed.code });
      return;
    }
    const entries = listed.entries.sort((a, b) => compareCodeUnits(a.name, b.name));
    const inMigrationPackage = entries.some(
      (entry) => entry.name === 'migration.json' && isFileEntry(dir, entry),
    );
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const path = join(dir, entry.name);
      if (entry.name.endsWith(TEMPORARY_SUFFIX)) {
        leftovers.push(path);
        continue;
      }
      if (entry.isDirectory() || (entry.isSymbolicLink() && isDirectory(path))) {
        if (!SKIPPED_DIRECTORIES.has(entry.name) && !entry.name.startsWith('.')) visit(path);
        continue;
      }
      if (!isFileEntry(dir, entry)) continue;
      const realFile = realpathSync(path);
      const linked = entry.isSymbolicLink();
      const known = found.get(realFile);
      if (known === undefined || (known.linked && !linked))
        found.set(realFile, { path, linked, inMigrationPackage });
    }
  };
  visit(root);
  const files = [...found.values()];
  const named = (test: (file: FoundFile, name: string) => boolean): string[] =>
    files.filter((file) => test(file, basename(file.path))).map((file) => file.path);
  return {
    json: named((_file, name) => name.endsWith('.json')),
    migrationJson: named((_file, name) => name === 'migration.json'),
    refs: named((file, name) => name.endsWith('.json') && basename(dirname(file.path)) === 'refs'),
    migrationTs: named((file, name) => name === 'migration.ts' && file.inMigrationPackage),
    leftovers,
    unreadable,
  };
}

type DirectoryListing =
  | { readonly ok: true; readonly entries: Dirent[] }
  | { readonly ok: false; readonly code: string };

function listDirectory(dir: string): DirectoryListing {
  try {
    return { ok: true, entries: readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }) };
  } catch (error) {
    const code = error instanceof Error && 'code' in error ? String(error.code) : 'unknown error';
    return { ok: false, code };
  }
}

function isSnapshotContract(path: string): boolean {
  const snapshotDir = dirname(path);
  return (
    basename(path) === 'contract.json' &&
    HASH.test(basename(snapshotDir)) &&
    basename(dirname(snapshotDir)) === 'snapshots'
  );
}

function replaceQuotedHashes(text: string, hashes: ReadonlyMap<string, string>): string {
  return text.replace(/"([0-9a-f]{64})"/g, (match: string, hash: string) => {
    const next = hashes.get(hash);
    return next === undefined ? match : `"${next}"`;
  });
}

function replaceHashTokens(text: string, hashes: ReadonlyMap<string, string>): string {
  return text.replace(
    /(?<![0-9a-f])[0-9a-f]{64}(?![0-9a-f])/g,
    (hash: string) => hashes.get(hash) ?? hash,
  );
}

function readDirectory(dir: string): Map<string, string> {
  const files = new Map<string, string>();
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return files;
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }))
    if (isFileEntry(dir, entry) && !entry.name.endsWith(TEMPORARY_SUFFIX))
      files.set(entry.name, readFileSync(join(dir, entry.name), 'utf8'));
  return files;
}

function sameFiles(a: ReadonlyMap<string, string>, b: ReadonlyMap<string, string>): boolean {
  return a.size === b.size && [...a].every(([name, content]) => b.get(name) === content);
}

function temporaryPath(path: string): string {
  return join(dirname(path), `.${basename(path)}${TEMPORARY_SUFFIX}`);
}

function writeWithModeOf(path: string, text: string, modeSource: string): void {
  writeFileSync(path, text);
  if (existsSync(modeSource)) chmodSync(path, statSync(modeSource).mode & 0o7777);
}

function writeFile(path: string, text: string): void {
  const target = realpathSync(path);
  const temporary = temporaryPath(target);
  writeWithModeOf(temporary, text, target);
  renameSync(temporary, target);
}

function writeDirectory(dir: string, files: ReadonlyMap<string, string>, sourceDir: string): void {
  const temporary = temporaryPath(dir);
  mkdirSync(temporary);
  for (const [name, text] of files)
    writeWithModeOf(join(temporary, name), text, join(sourceDir, name));
  renameSync(temporary, dir);
}

function removeDirectory(dir: string): void {
  const temporary = temporaryPath(dir);
  renameSync(dir, temporary);
  rmSync(temporary, { recursive: true, force: true });
}

function count(amount: number, singular: string, plural: string): string {
  return `${amount} ${amount === 1 ? singular : plural}`;
}

function recordsOf(value: Json | undefined): [string, JsonRecord][] {
  return isRecord(value)
    ? Object.entries(value).filter((entry): entry is [string, JsonRecord] => isRecord(entry[1]))
    : [];
}

function coordinate(namespaceId: string, entityKind: string, entityName: string): JsonRecord {
  return { plane: 'storage', namespaceId, entityKind, entityName };
}

interface Rewrite {
  readonly contract: JsonRecord;
  readonly changed: boolean;
  /** The storage namespace each moved value object now lives in, by name. */
  readonly valueObjectNamespaces: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
  readonly problems: readonly string[];
}

/** Whether the contract keeps value objects in the domain plane, or refers to one by name. */
function holdsOldValueObjects(contract: JsonRecord): boolean {
  const domain = isRecord(contract['domain']) ? contract['domain'] : {};
  for (const [, namespace] of recordsOf(domain['namespaces'])) {
    if (Object.hasOwn(namespace, 'valueObjects')) return true;
    for (const [, model] of recordsOf(namespace['models']))
      for (const [, field] of recordsOf(model['fields'])) {
        const type = field['type'];
        if (isRecord(type) && type['kind'] === 'valueObject' && typeof type['name'] === 'string')
          return true;
      }
  }
  return false;
}

/** A field that names a value object by `name`, pointed at it by its storage coordinate. */
function withValueObjectCoordinate(
  field: JsonRecord,
  namespaceOf: (name: string) => string | undefined,
  where: string,
  problems: string[],
): JsonRecord {
  const type = field['type'];
  if (!isRecord(type) || type['kind'] !== 'valueObject' || typeof type['name'] !== 'string')
    return field;
  const namespaceId = namespaceOf(type['name']);
  if (namespaceId === undefined) {
    problems.push(
      `${where} holds the value object ${type['name']}, which the contract does not declare`,
    );
    return field;
  }
  return {
    ...field,
    type: { kind: 'valueObject', ...coordinate(namespaceId, 'valueObject', type['name']) },
  };
}

function valueSetsOf(storageNamespace: JsonRecord): JsonRecord {
  const entries = isRecord(storageNamespace['entries']) ? storageNamespace['entries'] : {};
  return isRecord(entries['valueSet']) ? entries['valueSet'] : {};
}

/** The old MongoDB schema let a member leave `nullable` out, meaning `false`, and say `dict: false`; storage requires `nullable` and keeps `dict` only when it is `true`. */
function withStorageModifiers(member: JsonRecord): JsonRecord {
  const { dict, ...rest } = member;
  return {
    ...rest,
    nullable: member['nullable'] === undefined ? false : member['nullable'],
    ...(dict === undefined || dict === false ? {} : { dict }),
  };
}

/** A value object member, with an enum reference pointed at the enum's storage value set. */
function rewrittenMember(
  stored: JsonRecord,
  storageNamespaces: JsonRecord,
  where: string,
  problems: string[],
): JsonRecord {
  const member = withStorageModifiers(stored);
  const valueSet = member['valueSet'];
  if (!isRecord(valueSet) || valueSet['plane'] === 'storage') return member;
  const namespaceId = valueSet['namespaceId'];
  const name = valueSet['entityName'];
  const storageNamespace =
    typeof namespaceId === 'string' ? storageNamespaces[namespaceId] : undefined;
  if (
    typeof namespaceId !== 'string' ||
    typeof name !== 'string' ||
    !isRecord(storageNamespace) ||
    !Object.hasOwn(valueSetsOf(storageNamespace), name)
  ) {
    problems.push(
      `${where} is typed by the enum ${String(name)}, which has no value set in storage namespace ${String(namespaceId)}`,
    );
    return member;
  }
  return { ...member, valueSet: { ...valueSet, ...coordinate(namespaceId, 'valueSet', name) } };
}

/** Writes each discriminator's value set, `<Base>.<field>`, in its base table's namespace, and points the column at it, unless an enum already types the column. */
function writeDiscriminatorValueSets(
  domainNamespaces: JsonRecord,
  storageNamespaces: JsonRecord,
  problems: string[],
): boolean {
  let changed = false;
  for (const [modelNamespaceId, namespace] of recordsOf(domainNamespaces)) {
    for (const [modelName, model] of recordsOf(namespace['models'])) {
      const discriminator = model['discriminator'];
      const variants = model['variants'];
      const storage = model['storage'];
      if (!isRecord(discriminator) || !isRecord(variants) || !isRecord(storage)) continue;
      const field = discriminator['field'];
      const fields = isRecord(storage['fields']) ? storage['fields'] : {};
      const fieldStorage = typeof field === 'string' ? fields[field] : undefined;
      const columnName = isRecord(fieldStorage) ? fieldStorage['column'] : undefined;
      const tableName = storage['table'];
      const namespaceId =
        typeof storage['namespaceId'] === 'string' ? storage['namespaceId'] : modelNamespaceId;
      const storageNamespace = storageNamespaces[namespaceId];
      const entries = isRecord(storageNamespace) ? storageNamespace['entries'] : undefined;
      const tables = isRecord(entries) ? entries['table'] : undefined;
      const table =
        isRecord(tables) && typeof tableName === 'string' ? tables[tableName] : undefined;
      const columns = isRecord(table) ? table['columns'] : undefined;
      const column =
        isRecord(columns) && typeof columnName === 'string' ? columns[columnName] : undefined;
      if (
        typeof field !== 'string' ||
        typeof columnName !== 'string' ||
        !isRecord(entries) ||
        !isRecord(columns) ||
        !isRecord(column) ||
        column['valueSet'] !== undefined
      )
        continue;
      const name = `${modelName}.${field}`;
      const valueSets = isRecord(entries['valueSet']) ? entries['valueSet'] : {};
      if (Object.hasOwn(valueSets, name)) {
        problems.push(
          `the discriminator ${name} writes the value set ${name} in storage namespace ${namespaceId}, which already holds a value set of that name; rename the enum`,
        );
        continue;
      }
      entries['valueSet'] = {
        ...valueSets,
        [name]: { kind: 'valueSet', values: Object.keys(variants).sort(compareCodeUnits) },
      };
      columns[columnName] = { ...column, valueSet: coordinate(namespaceId, 'valueSet', name) };
      changed = true;
    }
  }
  return changed;
}

/** The contract with its value objects moved into storage, and on SQL each discriminator's value set written. */
function rewriteContract(contract: JsonRecord, family: Family): Rewrite {
  const unchanged: Rewrite = {
    contract,
    changed: false,
    valueObjectNamespaces: new Map(),
    problems: [],
  };
  if (!holdsOldValueObjects(contract)) return unchanged;
  const copy = parseJson(JSON.stringify(contract));
  if (!isRecord(copy) || !isRecord(copy['domain']) || !isRecord(copy['storage'])) return unchanged;
  const domainNamespaces = isRecord(copy['domain']['namespaces'])
    ? copy['domain']['namespaces']
    : {};
  const storageNamespaces = isRecord(copy['storage']['namespaces'])
    ? copy['storage']['namespaces']
    : {};
  const problems: string[] = [];
  const valueObjectNamespaces = new Map<string, string>();
  const declaredIn = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  for (const [namespaceId, namespace] of recordsOf(domainNamespaces))
    for (const [name] of recordsOf(namespace['valueObjects']))
      declaredIn.set(name, new Set([...(declaredIn.get(name) ?? []), namespaceId]));
  const namespaceFor =
    (ownNamespaceId: string) =>
    (name: string): string | undefined => {
      const namespaces = declaredIn.get(name);
      if (namespaces === undefined) return undefined;
      if (namespaces.has(ownNamespaceId)) return ownNamespaceId;
      return namespaces.size === 1 ? [...namespaces][0] : undefined;
    };

  for (const [namespaceId, namespace] of recordsOf(domainNamespaces)) {
    const valueObjects = namespace['valueObjects'];
    delete namespace['valueObjects'];
    for (const [modelName, model] of recordsOf(namespace['models'])) {
      const fields = model['fields'];
      for (const [fieldName, field] of recordsOf(fields))
        if (isRecord(fields))
          fields[fieldName] = withValueObjectCoordinate(
            field,
            namespaceFor(namespaceId),
            `field ${modelName}.${fieldName}`,
            problems,
          );
    }
    if (!isRecord(valueObjects)) continue;
    const storageNamespace = storageNamespaces[namespaceId];
    if (!isRecord(storageNamespace)) {
      problems.push(
        `the value objects of domain namespace ${namespaceId} have no storage namespace ${namespaceId} to move to`,
      );
      continue;
    }
    const moved: JsonRecord = {};
    for (const [name, valueObject] of recordsOf(valueObjects)) {
      valueObjectNamespaces.set(name, namespaceId);
      const members: JsonRecord = {};
      for (const [memberName, member] of recordsOf(valueObject['fields'])) {
        const where = `value object member ${name}.${memberName}`;
        members[memberName] = rewrittenMember(
          withValueObjectCoordinate(member, namespaceFor(namespaceId), where, problems),
          storageNamespaces,
          where,
          problems,
        );
      }
      moved[name] = { ...valueObject, fields: members };
    }
    const entries = isRecord(storageNamespace['entries']) ? storageNamespace['entries'] : {};
    storageNamespace['entries'] = { ...entries, valueObject: moved };
  }
  if (family === 'sql') writeDiscriminatorValueSets(domainNamespaces, storageNamespaces, problems);
  if (Object.hasOwn(copy, 'valueObjects')) delete copy['valueObjects'];
  return { contract: copy, changed: true, valueObjectNamespaces, problems };
}

function withStorageHash(contract: JsonRecord, hash: string): JsonRecord {
  const storage = contract['storage'];
  if (!isRecord(storage) || typeof storage['storageHash'] !== 'string') return contract;
  return { ...contract, storage: { ...storage, storageHash: hash } };
}

function lineEndingOf(text: string): string {
  return text.includes('\r\n') ? '\r\n' : '\n';
}

/** The contract written the way the file held it: a snapshot's canonical line, or indented JSON, with the file's byte order mark and line ending. */
function writtenForm(contract: JsonRecord, original: JsonRecord, text: string): string {
  const mark = text.startsWith(BYTE_ORDER_MARK) ? BYTE_ORDER_MARK : '';
  const body = withoutByteOrderMark(text);
  const lineEnding = lineEndingOf(body);
  const finalNewline = body.endsWith('\n') ? lineEnding : '';
  if (body === `${canonicalizeJson(original)}${finalNewline}`)
    return `${mark}${canonicalizeJson(contract)}${finalNewline}`;
  const indented = JSON.stringify(contract, null, 2).replaceAll('\n', lineEnding);
  return `${mark}${indented}${finalNewline}`;
}

interface Block {
  readonly start: number;
  end: number;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly parent: Block | undefined;
}

function scanBlocks(text: string): Block[] {
  const blocks: Block[] = [];
  const open: Block[] = [];
  let quote: string | undefined;
  for (let index = 0; index < text.length; index++) {
    const char = text[index];
    if (quote !== undefined) {
      if (char === '\\') index++;
      else if (char === quote) quote = undefined;
      continue;
    }
    if (char === '/' && text[index + 1] === '/') {
      const end = text.indexOf('\n', index);
      index = end === -1 ? text.length : end;
      continue;
    }
    if (char === '/' && text[index + 1] === '*') {
      const end = text.indexOf('*/', index + 2);
      index = end === -1 ? text.length : end + 1;
      continue;
    }
    if (char === "'" || char === '"' || char === '`') {
      quote = char;
      continue;
    }
    if (char === '{') {
      const key =
        /(?:readonly\s+)?([\p{ID_Start}_$][\p{ID_Continue}$]*|'[^']*'|"[^"]*")\s*\??\s*:\s*$/u.exec(
          text.slice(Math.max(0, index - 200), index),
        );
      const block: Block = {
        start: index,
        end: text.length,
        label: key?.[1]?.replace(/^['"]|['"]$/g, '') ?? '',
        parent: open.at(-1),
      };
      open.push(block);
      blocks.push(block);
    } else if (char === '}') {
      const block = open.pop();
      if (block !== undefined) block.end = index;
    }
  }
  return blocks;
}

function lineStart(text: string, position: number): number {
  return text.lastIndexOf('\n', position - 1) + 1;
}

/** The end of the member a block closes: past its `;` and the line break after it. */
function memberEnd(text: string, block: Block): number {
  const rest = /^\s*;?[ \t]*(?:\r?\n)?/.exec(text.slice(block.end + 1));
  return block.end + 1 + (rest?.[0].length ?? 0);
}

function indentOf(text: string, position: number): string {
  return /^[ \t]*/.exec(text.slice(lineStart(text, position)))?.[0] ?? '';
}

function childBlocks(blocks: readonly Block[], parent: Block): Block[] {
  return blocks.filter((block) => block.parent === parent);
}

function isUnder(block: Block, labels: readonly string[]): boolean {
  let current = block.parent;
  for (const label of labels) {
    if (current?.label !== label) return false;
    current = current.parent;
  }
  return true;
}

/** A block re-indented from `from` to `to`, its first line left as it starts. */
function reindent(literal: string, from: string, to: string): string {
  return literal
    .split('\n')
    .map((line, index) =>
      index === 0 || !line.startsWith(from) ? line : `${to}${line.slice(from.length)}`,
    )
    .join('\n');
}

interface Edit {
  readonly start: number;
  readonly end: number;
  readonly text: string;
}

const STORAGE_NAMESPACES = "ContractBase['storage']['namespaces']";

function dtsPathOf(contractPath: string, snapshot: boolean): string {
  return snapshot
    ? join(dirname(contractPath), 'contract.d.ts')
    : `${contractPath.slice(0, -'.json'.length)}.d.ts`;
}
const DTS_LINE_WIDTH = 100;

/**
 * The same move in `contract.d.ts`: each `valueObjects` type of a domain namespace goes into its storage namespace's `entries` as `valueObject`, a member's enum reference names the storage value set, a field's value object type names its coordinate, the top-level `valueObjects` type goes, and the value object and field type aliases read storage. The discriminator value sets are not typed: a re-emit types them.
 */
function rewriteDts(
  text: string,
  valueObjectNamespaces: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
  hashes: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
): string {
  const lineEnding = lineEndingOf(text);
  const blocks = scanBlocks(text);
  const edits: Edit[] = [];
  const moved = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const block of blocks) {
    if (block.label !== 'valueObjects') continue;
    const namespace = block.parent;
    if (namespace !== undefined && isUnder(namespace, ['namespaces', 'domain'])) {
      const literal = text
        .slice(block.start, block.end + 1)
        .replace(/readonly plane: (['"])domain\1/g, "readonly plane: 'storage'")
        .replace(/readonly entityKind: (['"])enum\1/g, "readonly entityKind: 'valueSet'");
      moved.set(namespace.label, reindent(literal, indentOf(text, block.start), ''));
      edits.push({ start: lineStart(text, block.start), end: memberEnd(text, block), text: '' });
    } else if (
      namespace !== undefined &&
      childBlocks(blocks, namespace).some((sibling) => sibling.label === 'domain')
    ) {
      edits.push({ start: lineStart(text, block.start), end: memberEnd(text, block), text: '' });
    }
  }
  for (const block of blocks) {
    if (block.label !== 'entries' || block.parent === undefined) continue;
    if (!isUnder(block.parent, ['namespaces']) || isUnder(block.parent, ['namespaces', 'domain']))
      continue;
    const literal = moved.get(block.parent.label);
    if (literal === undefined) continue;
    const indent = `${indentOf(text, block.start)}  `;
    const closing = lineStart(text, block.end);
    edits.push({
      start: closing,
      end: closing,
      text: `${indent}readonly valueObject: ${reindent(literal, '', indent)};${lineEnding}`,
    });
  }
  let result = text;
  for (const edit of edits.sort((a, b) => b.start - a.start))
    result = `${result.slice(0, edit.start)}${edit.text}${result.slice(edit.end)}`;
  result = result
    .replace(
      /\{\s*readonly kind: (['"])valueObject\1;\s*readonly name: (['"])([^'"]*)\2;?\s*\}/g,
      (
        match: string,
        _quote: string,
        _nameQuote: string,
        name: string,
        offset: number,
        whole: string,
      ) => {
        const namespaceId = valueObjectNamespaces.get(name);
        return namespaceId === undefined
          ? match
          : coordinateTypeLiteral(namespaceId, name, whole, offset, lineEnding);
      },
    )
    .replace(
      /ValueObjectTypesFromDomain<(\s*)ContractBase\['domain'\]\['namespaces'\]/g,
      `ValueObjectTypesFromStorage<$1${STORAGE_NAMESPACES}`,
    )
    .replace(/\bValueObjectTypesFromDomain\b/g, 'ValueObjectTypesFromStorage');
  return replaceHashTokens(withStorageNamespacesArgument(result), hashes);
}

/** `FieldTypesFromDomain` with the storage namespaces as its sixth argument, which it now requires of every contract. */
function withStorageNamespacesArgument(text: string): string {
  const lineEnding = lineEndingOf(text);
  return text.replace(
    /(FieldTypesFromDomain<[^<>]*?(['"])(?:output|input)\2)(\s*)>/g,
    (_match: string, head: string, _quote: string, space: string) =>
      space.includes('\n')
        ? `${head},${lineEnding}  ${STORAGE_NAMESPACES}${lineEnding}>`
        : `${head}, ${STORAGE_NAMESPACES}>`,
  );
}

/** A value object field's coordinate type, on one line when it fits the emitter's line width, else one member per line. */
function coordinateTypeLiteral(
  namespaceId: string,
  name: string,
  text: string,
  offset: number,
  lineEnding: string,
): string {
  const members = [
    "readonly kind: 'valueObject'",
    "readonly plane: 'storage'",
    `readonly namespaceId: '${namespaceId}'`,
    "readonly entityKind: 'valueObject'",
    `readonly entityName: '${name}'`,
  ];
  const single = `{ ${members.join('; ')} }`;
  if (offset - lineStart(text, offset) + single.length + 1 <= DTS_LINE_WIDTH) return single;
  const indent = indentOf(text, offset);
  const lines = members.map((member) => `${indent}  ${member};`);
  return `{${lineEnding}${lines.join(lineEnding)}${lineEnding}${indent}}`;
}

interface ContractPlan {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly snapshot: boolean;
  readonly oldHash: string;
  readonly newHash: string;
  readonly content: string;
  readonly valueObjectNamespaces: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
}

interface MigrationOps {
  readonly path: string;
  /** `undefined` when the package has no `ops.json` or it is not valid JSON. */
  readonly ops: Json | undefined;
  readonly unreadable: boolean;
}

function readOps(migrationDir: string): MigrationOps {
  const path = join(migrationDir, 'ops.json');
  if (!existsSync(path)) return { path, ops: undefined, unreadable: false };
  const ops = parseJson(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
  return { path, ops, unreadable: ops === undefined };
}

function familyOf(contract: JsonRecord): Family | undefined {
  const family = contract['targetFamily'];
  return family === 'sql' || family === 'mongo' ? family : undefined;
}

function summary(
  root: string,
  contractsFound: number,
  files: number,
  directories: number,
  hashes: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
): readonly string[] {
  if (contractsFound === 0)
    return [`No SQL or MongoDB contract was found under ${root}; nothing changed.`];
  if (files === 0 && directories === 0)
    return ['No contract keeps value objects in the domain plane; nothing changed.'];
  const renamed = count(directories, 'snapshot directory', 'snapshot directories');
  const changes = `Rewrote ${count(files, 'file', 'files')} and renamed ${renamed}.`;
  if (hashes.size === 0) return [changes];
  return [
    `${changes} Storage hashes changed (old -> new):`,
    ...[...hashes]
      .sort(([a], [b]) => compareCodeUnits(a, b))
      .map(([oldHash, newHash]) => `  ${oldHash} -> ${newHash}`),
  ];
}

const JSON_FILES_THAT_MUST_PARSE = new Set(['contract.json', 'migration.json']);

function main({
  root,
  errors,
}: {
  readonly root: string;
  readonly errors: readonly string[];
}): number {
  if (errors.length > 0) {
    process.stderr.write(`${errors.join('\n')}\n`);
    return 1;
  }
  const display = (path: string): string => relative(root, path).split(sep).join('/');
  const files = listFiles(root);
  if (files.unreadable.length > 0) {
    process.stderr.write(
      `${files.unreadable
        .map(
          ({ dir, code }) =>
            `${display(dir)}: cannot read the directory (${code}); give the script read access to it, or move it out of the project, and run the script again`,
        )
        .join('\n')}\n`,
    );
    return 1;
  }
  const plans: ContractPlan[] = [];
  const argumentWrites = new Map<string, string>();
  const stops: string[] = [];
  let contractsFound = 0;

  for (const path of files.json) {
    const text = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
    const contract = parseJson(text);
    if (
      contract === undefined &&
      (JSON_FILES_THAT_MUST_PARSE.has(basename(path)) || files.refs.includes(path))
    ) {
      stops.push(`${display(path)}: not valid JSON`);
      continue;
    }
    if (!isRecord(contract) || typeof contract['target'] !== 'string') continue;
    const family = familyOf(contract);
    if (family === undefined || !isRecord(contract['storage'])) continue;
    contractsFound++;
    const rewrite = rewriteContract(contract, family);
    const snapshot = isSnapshotContract(path);
    if (!rewrite.changed) {
      const dtsPath = dtsPathOf(path, snapshot);
      if (existsSync(dtsPath)) {
        const dts = readFileSync(dtsPath, 'utf8');
        const next = withStorageNamespacesArgument(dts);
        if (next !== dts) argumentWrites.set(dtsPath, next);
      }
      continue;
    }
    const stored = contract['storage']['storageHash'];
    const oldHash = snapshot ? basename(dirname(path)) : typeof stored === 'string' ? stored : '';
    const computed = computeStorageHash(family, contract);
    if (computed !== oldHash || (typeof stored === 'string' && stored !== oldHash)) {
      stops.push(
        `${display(path)}: the stored storage hash ${oldHash} does not match the contract's content, which hashes to ${computed}; restore the file from version control, or re-emit it, and run the script again`,
      );
      continue;
    }
    if (rewrite.problems.length > 0) {
      for (const problem of rewrite.problems)
        stops.push(
          `${display(path)}: ${problem}; restore the file from version control, or re-emit it, and run the script again`,
        );
      continue;
    }
    const newHash = computeStorageHash(family, rewrite.contract);
    plans.push({
      path,
      snapshot,
      oldHash,
      newHash,
      content: writtenForm(withStorageHash(rewrite.contract, newHash), contract, text),
      valueObjectNamespaces: rewrite.valueObjectNamespaces,
    });
  }

  const hashes = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const plan of [...plans].sort((a, b) => Number(b.snapshot) - Number(a.snapshot)))
    if (plan.oldHash !== plan.newHash && !hashes.has(plan.oldHash))
      hashes.set(plan.oldHash, plan.newHash);

  const newDirectories = new Map<string, Map<string, string>>();
  const directorySources = new Map<string, string>();
  const sourceDirectories = new Set<string>();
  const removals = new Set<string>();
  const snapshotRewrites: [string, string][] = [];
  const referenceWrites = new Map<string, string>();
  const contractWrites = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const plan of plans) {
    const dtsPath = dtsPathOf(plan.path, plan.snapshot);
    const dtsHashes = new Map([...hashes, [plan.oldHash, plan.newHash]]);
    const dts = existsSync(dtsPath)
      ? rewriteDts(readFileSync(dtsPath, 'utf8'), plan.valueObjectNamespaces, dtsHashes)
      : undefined;
    if (!plan.snapshot) {
      if (dts !== undefined) referenceWrites.set(dtsPath, dts);
      contractWrites.set(plan.path, plan.content);
      continue;
    }
    const oldDir = dirname(plan.path);
    const newDir = join(dirname(oldDir), plan.newHash);
    sourceDirectories.add(oldDir);
    if (newDir === oldDir) {
      if (dts !== undefined) snapshotRewrites.push([dtsPath, dts]);
      snapshotRewrites.push([plan.path, plan.content]);
      continue;
    }
    removals.add(oldDir);
    const content = readDirectory(oldDir);
    content.set('contract.json', plan.content);
    if (dts !== undefined) content.set('contract.d.ts', dts);
    const planned = newDirectories.get(newDir);
    if (planned !== undefined && !sameFiles(planned, content)) {
      stops.push(`${display(newDir)}: snapshot directory already exists with different content`);
      continue;
    }
    newDirectories.set(newDir, content);
    directorySources.set(newDir, oldDir);
  }
  for (const [dir, content] of newDirectories) {
    if (sourceDirectories.has(dir) || !existsSync(dir)) continue;
    if (sameFiles(readDirectory(dir), content)) newDirectories.delete(dir);
    else stops.push(`${display(dir)}: snapshot directory already exists with different content`);
  }

  for (const path of files.migrationJson) {
    const text = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
    const metadata = parseJson(text);
    if (!isRecord(metadata)) continue;
    const from = metadata['from'];
    const to = metadata['to'];
    const nextFrom = typeof from === 'string' ? (hashes.get(from) ?? from) : from;
    const nextTo = typeof to === 'string' ? (hashes.get(to) ?? to) : to;
    if (nextFrom === from && nextTo === to) continue;
    const { path: opsPath, ops, unreadable } = readOps(dirname(path));
    if (unreadable) {
      stops.push(`${display(opsPath)}: not valid JSON`);
      continue;
    }
    const oldMigrationHash = metadata['migrationHash'];
    let next = replaceQuotedHashes(text, hashes);
    if (
      ops !== undefined &&
      typeof oldMigrationHash === 'string' &&
      nextFrom !== undefined &&
      nextTo !== undefined
    ) {
      const migrationHash = computeMigrationHash({ ...metadata, from: nextFrom, to: nextTo }, ops);
      next = next.replace(`"${oldMigrationHash}"`, `"${migrationHash}"`);
    }
    referenceWrites.set(path, next);
  }
  for (const path of files.refs) {
    const text = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
    const next = replaceQuotedHashes(text, hashes);
    if (next !== text) referenceWrites.set(path, next);
  }
  for (const path of files.migrationTs) {
    const text = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
    const next = replaceHashTokens(text, hashes);
    if (next !== text) referenceWrites.set(path, next);
  }

  if (stops.length > 0) {
    process.stderr.write(`${[...new Set(stops)].join('\n')}\n`);
    return 1;
  }

  try {
    for (const path of files.leftovers) rmSync(path, { recursive: true, force: true });
    for (const [dir, content] of newDirectories)
      writeDirectory(dir, content, directorySources.get(dir) ?? dir);
    for (const [path, text] of snapshotRewrites) writeFile(path, text);
    for (const [path, text] of referenceWrites) writeFile(path, text);
    for (const [path, text] of contractWrites) writeFile(path, text);
    for (const [path, text] of argumentWrites) writeFile(path, text);
    for (const dir of removals) removeDirectory(dir);
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    process.stderr.write(
      `${message}; the upgrade stopped partway, run the script again to finish it\n`,
    );
    return 1;
  }
  const rewrittenFiles =
    snapshotRewrites.length + referenceWrites.size + contractWrites.size + argumentWrites.size;
  const lines = summary(root, contractsFound, rewrittenFiles, removals.size, hashes);
  process.stdout.write(`${lines.join('\n')}\n`);
  return 0;
}

function parseRoot(args: readonly string[]): { readonly root: string; readonly errors: string[] } {
  const errors = args.filter((arg) => arg.startsWith('-')).map((arg) => `${arg}: unknown option`);
  const positional = args.filter((arg) => !arg.startsWith('-'));
  if (positional.length > 1) errors.push(`expected one project root, got ${positional.length}`);
  const root = resolve(positional[0] ?? process.cwd());
  if (errors.length === 0 && !isDirectory(root)) errors.push(`${root}: not a directory`);
  if (errors.length > 0) errors.push('Usage: node value-objects-in-storage.ts [project-root]');
  return { root, errors };
}

process.exitCode = main(parseRoot(process.argv.slice(2)));
````

---
from: "8.0.0-rc.21"
to: "8.0.0-rc.22"
changes:
  - id: one-orm-version
    summary: |
      Every `@prisma/orm-*` package and the `prisma` CLI must run one version of Prisma ORM. In 8.0.0-rc.22, commands and clients stop with `RUNTIME.MULTIPLE_ORM_COPIES` when more than one copy is installed; later releases remove that check, but a second copy still breaks values that cross between copies.
    detection:
      glob: "package.json"
      matches:
        - '"@prisma/orm-'
  - id: value-objects-in-storage
    summary: |
      A contract keeps its value objects in storage, at `storage.namespaces.<ns>.entries.valueObject`, and a field holding one names it by its storage coordinate. On SQL, a discriminator column names a value set, `<Base>.<field>`, of its variants' values. A `contract.json` that keeps `valueObjects` in the domain plane is refused with `CONTRACT.VALIDATION_FAILED`, saying to re-emit it. Run the colocated script on the project: it rewrites every contract and snapshot, renames the snapshot directories to their new storage hashes, and rewrites the migrations, refs, `migration.ts` files and `contract.d.ts` files that name them. Then sign each database and re-emit the contract.
    detection:
      glob: "**/*.json"
      matches:
        - '"valueObjects"\s*:'
    script: ./scripts/value-objects-in-storage/value-objects-in-storage.ts
  - id: value-object-types-from-storage
    summary: |
      `ValueObjectTypesFromDomain`, exported by `@prisma/orm-mongo/contract/types`, is now `ValueObjectTypesFromStorage` and takes the contract's storage namespaces. A committed `contract.d.ts` that imports it compiles again once it is re-emitted. Code of your own that imports it changes the name and passes `Contract['storage']['namespaces']`.
    detection:
      glob: "**/*.{ts,mts,cts,tsx}"
      matches:
        - '\bValueObjectTypesFromDomain\b'
  - id: postgres-value-object-checks
    summary: |
      On PostgreSQL, the contract derives a check for every value object column and every discriminator column of a managed table. The next `prisma migration plan` adds them, and `prisma db migrate` fails on a row that does not fit, including a row whose value object has a key the value object does not declare, which the SQL ORM never refused. Find such rows before you apply the migration.
  - id: discriminator-typed-by-variant-values
    summary: |
      A SQL discriminator field is typed by its variants' values, such as `'bug' | 'feature'`, instead of `string`. Code that assigns such a field to a `string` still compiles; a type assertion that expects `string` changes to the union.
  - id: psl-date-time-types-are-convenience-types
    summary: |
      In a Prisma 8 schema on PostgreSQL, `DateTime`, `Date` and `Time` are now convenience types that choose an explicit type from their arguments, and their defaults read different values: `DateTime` is a `timestamptz(3)` column read as a JavaScript `Date`, and `Date` and `Time` are read as strings. To keep what a field reads today, and its contract, rename `DateTime` to `TimestamptzTemporal`, `Date` to `DateTemporal` and `Time` to `TimeTemporal`, keeping the arguments: `Time(3)` becomes `TimeTemporal(3)`. A Prisma 7 schema, which has a `datasource` block, and SQLite and MongoDB schemas are not affected.
    detection:
      glob: "**/*.prisma"
      matches:
        - '(?<![\s\S])(?![\s\S]*(?<![\w$])datasource[ \t]+\w+[ \t]*\{)[\s\S]*\n[ \t]+[A-Za-z_]\w*[ \t]+(?:=[ \t]*)?(?:DateTime|Date|Time)(?![\w$])'
  - id: ts-date-time-helpers-are-convenience-types
    summary: |
      In a TypeScript contract on PostgreSQL, `type.DateTime(...)`, `type.Date(...)` and `type.Time(...)` are now the convenience types, whose arguments are one object with the keys `as`, `storage` and `precision`, so `type.Time(3)` no longer compiles. To keep what a field reads today, call `type.TimestamptzTemporal(...)`, `type.DateTemporal()` and `type.TimeTemporal(...)` with the same arguments.
    detection:
      glob: "**/*.{ts,mts,cts,tsx}"
      matches:
        - '(?<![\w$])type\.(?:DateTime|Date|Time)\('
  - id: prisma7-schema-reads-dates
    summary: |
      A contract from `prisma7Schema(...)` on PostgreSQL now reads a Prisma 7 `DateTime` field as a JavaScript `Date`, as Prisma 7 did, instead of a string: a plain `DateTime` is `TimestampJsDate(3)` and a `@db.Timestamptz(p)` field is `TimestamptzJsDate(p)`. The columns do not change, but the contract's codecs and storage hash do. Re-emit with `prisma contract emit`, run `prisma db sign`, and change application code that read those fields as strings to read a `Date`.
    detection:
      glob: "**/prisma.config.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs}"
      matches:
        - '\bprisma7Schema\s*\('
  - id: temporal-type-aliases-on-datetime
    summary: |
      On PostgreSQL, `temporal.CreatedAt` and `temporal.UpdatedAt` are now built on `DateTime`, a `timestamptz(3)` column read as a JavaScript `Date`, instead of a `timestamptz` column read as a `Temporal.Instant`, and the `temporal.CreatedAtString`, `temporal.UpdatedAtString`, `temporal.CreatedAtJsDate` and `temporal.UpdatedAtJsDate` aliases are removed, in PSL and as `type.temporal.*()` in a TypeScript contract. Write the type and the generators instead, as the table in the body shows, to keep each field and its contract.
    detection:
      glob: "**/*.{prisma,ts,mts,cts,tsx}"
      matches:
        - '(?<![\w$])temporal\.(?:Created|Updated)At(?:String|JsDate)?(?![\w$])'
  - id: date-default-below-a-millisecond
    summary: |
      On PostgreSQL and MySQL, a column read as a JavaScript `Date` (`DateTime` at its default, `TimestamptzJsDate`, `TimestampJsDate`, MySQL's `DateTime`) now refuses a `@default` with digits below a millisecond, which a `Date` cannot hold, and `prisma contract emit` reports it. Keep the default by changing the field to `DateTime(as: string)` or `DateTime(as: temporal)`, or by writing the default as a `sql` expression.
    detection:
      glob: "**/*.prisma"
      matches:

  - id: date-now-takes-column-precision
    summary: |
      On PostgreSQL, the `now` generator of a timestamp column read as a JavaScript `Date` (`DateTime`, `TimestamptzJsDate`, `TimestampJsDate`, `temporal.CreatedAt` and `temporal.UpdatedAt`) or as a `Temporal` value (`DateTime(as: temporal)`, `TimestamptzTemporal`, `TimestampTemporal` and `TimestampInstant`) now takes the column's precision and rounds the time down to it, so the value the client holds is the value PostgreSQL stores. A `timestamp(0)` column no longer gets a time PostgreSQL rounds up to the next second. The generator's precision is in the contract's execution section, so re-emit with `prisma contract emit` and commit `contract.json` and `contract.d.ts`; only the execution hash changes, so there is no migration and no `prisma db sign`.
    detection:
      glob: "**/*.{prisma,ts,mts,cts,tsx}"
      matches:
